caveat: Curated starting points for Lower Manhattan districts, with the Zoning Resolution sections to read. bulk.note: Bulk parameters read from the Zoning Resolution text at zr.planning.nyc.gov in October 2026, after the December 2024 renumbering of Article II Chapter 3. Every figure is a starting point to verify against the current text and the parcel's own conditions; null means the value could not be verified and was not guessed.

limitedHeightDistricts.condition: Applies only where the zoning lot does not contain qualifying affordable housing or qualifying senior housing.

notes: A wide street is 75 feet or more wide; a narrow street is less. PLUTO carries no street widths, so widths are inputs; when a width is missing the envelope uses the narrow-street rule and says so. ZR 12-10 lets some 65 to 75 foot portions of streets in C5-3, C6-4 and C6-6 count as wide; not encoded.

Optional bulk rules for sky exposure plane buildings in R6 through R10 districts without a letter suffix (ZR 23-05, 23-73, read Oct 23, 2026). Not in Limited Height Districts or R8 in Manhattan Community District 9 north of West 125th Street (ZR 23-731). Where elected, the height factor floor area ratio supersedes ZR 23-22 for every residence, including qualifying affordable and senior housing (ZR 23-732); heightFactor rows are [minimum open space ratio, maximum floor area ratio] for height factors 1 to 21; beyond 21 the ratio is what the required open space ratio allows, FAR = HF / (1 + HF x OSR / 100). Lot coverage limits need not apply (ZR 23-735); yards apply. In R9 and R10 a tower may penetrate the plane (ZR 23-737).

The corner portion is bounded by the intersecting street lines and lines parallel to and 100 feet from each; no rear yard is required there (read Oct 23, 2026). The rest of a corner lot is regulated as an interior or through lot portion. Beyond 100 feet of a street line, a side lot line counts as a rear lot line: a rear yard is required where it meets an adjoining rear lot line; in R6 to R12 none where it meets an adjoining side lot line, 5 feet in R1 to R5.
ZR 43-43 applies in every manufacturing district without an A suffix, so M1-5B is read with the M1-5 row; verify.
Alternative sky exposure plane building regulations of ZR 23-73; the standard R6 through R12 regime is the base height table of ZR 23-432.

A tower may penetrate the sky exposure plane when all buildings on the lot occupy at most the coverage. With deeper setbacks of 20 feet (narrow) and 15 feet (wide) the near-street caps rise to 2,250 and 2,000 square feet (ZR 33-451, second paragraph); not drawn.

Optional regime for lots bounded by two or more streets: coverage rises 0.5 percent for each 0.10 of FAR below the maximum, capped at 55 percent, with setbacks as fractions of the street wall width (at most 45 feet narrow, 35 feet wide). Reported, not drawn.
Alternative to the maximum building heights of ZR 23-432, above the district's maximum base height; the ZR 23-433 setback still applies to street walls above the maximum base height.

residentialTowerOnABase.appliesWhen: More than 25 percent of floor area is residential on a zoning lot fronting a wide street, within 125 feet of that frontage along the short block dimension or 100 feet along the long dimension, in R9 or R10 without a letter suffix (and C1-8, C1-9, C2-7, C2-8 or C1/C2 within R9 or R10).
notes: At 40 percent or more tower coverage, 55 percent of the floor area must be below 150 feet; the share rises 0.5 percent for each percent of coverage below 40, to 60 percent at 30 percent coverage. Reported as a check, not drawn.
Contextual district: one row for wide and narrow streets; eligible-site heights (ZR 23-434) apply only to districts without a letter suffix.
Outside Mandatory Inclusionary Housing areas, UAP developments within 100 feet of a wide street may use a 125 foot base and 175 foot building height (ZR 23-432 footnote 3).

Wide-street rows apply within 100 feet of a wide street; narrow-street rows beyond that. Lot coverage of 80 percent applies to interior and through lots, 100 percent to corner lots; eligible sites of 30,000 square feet or more are capped at 65 percent (ZR 23-362). In the Manhattan Core, ZR 35-631 line-up rules put the street wall on the street line along wide streets for R8 through R12 equivalents.

Commercial and community facility floors may occupy the 20 foot rear yard up to one storey and 23 feet. No rear yard within 100 feet of a corner. Through lots in C4-2 and higher, C5 and C6 need no rear yard equivalent. Commercial buildings have no lot coverage limit; residential portions follow the residential equivalent.

frontSetbackR1ThroughR5.skyExposurePlaneSlope: 1 vertical to 1 horizontal over the zoning lot, narrow and wide streets alike

frontSetbacksNonContextualR6Plus.note: ZR 24-522 as read 2026-10-30. The alternate front setbacks of ZR 24-53 (15/10 ft optional front open area, plane slopes 3.7/7.6) and the towers of ZR 24-54 (40% coverage, small-lot table) are not drawn.

3.note: Maximum base height is the default 85 feet or 1.5 times the street width, whichever is greater; minimum is 60 feet or five storeys.

notes: ZR 91-30 supersedes the underlying district height and setback rules; yards and floor area still come from the underlying district as modified by ZR 91-20. Street wall types come from Maps 2 and 3 and the Historic and Commercial Core from Map 1 in Appendix A; those maps are images and are not encoded, so the type and core membership are inputs. Where a lot fronts streets with different base heights, ZR 91-33 applies the coverage limits at a plane per base height; the envelope uses the lowest base height for the whole lot.

floorAreaExclusions.note: Floor space counted as zoning floor area and the exclusions a schematic plan can show; the rest of the ZR 12-10 list (bulkheads, uncovered steps, low attics, open balconies and terraces, Fire Department storage, rooftop greenhouses, electrified buildings) is not drawn by the planning engine.

counted.rule: Stairwells at each floor count, except the extra width excluded in buildings over 125 ft
Elevator shafts at each floor count

excluded.rule: Cellar space, except space used for dwelling purposes
Accessory mechanical equipment and the minimum space for its maintenance and access
Accessory off-street parking in group parking facilities no more than 23 ft above curb level
Residential amenities accessible to residents (recreation, co-working, package and storage rooms, laundry, pet facilities), up to 5 percent of the building's residential floor area

Half the floor space of a corridor that reaches the farthest dwelling unit door within 100 ft of the elevator core, or that has a balcony, 20 sq ft of daylight glazing, or ends at a unit of three or more bedrooms
Refuse storage and disposal, up to 3 sq ft per dwelling unit
Required enclosed bicycle parking, up to 15 sq ft per required space; one space per two dwelling units, waived at 10 units or fewer

noFactorIn: conversions of non-residential buildings in special density areas

inner.note: No accessory parking is required for dwelling units created after December 5, 2024 in the Inner Transit Zone.

outer.note: Reduced percent covers ancillary dwelling units, qualifying senior housing and income-restricted units in qualifying affordable housing. In the ZR tables a district named without a letter suffix includes its lettered variants where they are not listed separately.

beyond.note: Small lot means 10,000 sq ft or less; mid lot means 10,001 to 15,000 sq ft (ZR 25-232 footnotes).

notes: Every district in this table is in the Manhattan Core, where no parking is required. Requirements and transit-zone waivers outside the Manhattan Core (ZR 25-00 and the Greater, Inner and Outer Transit Zones) are not encoded; null means not verified.

mechanisms.name: Zoning lot merger
mechanisms.note: Unused floor area moves within a merged zoning lot of contiguous lots in the same block, by declaration recorded against every lot.

mechanisms.name: Landmark development rights transfer
mechanisms.note: Unused landmark floor area transfers by City Planning Commission Chair certification to receiving lots in the surrounding area (ZR 75-421), capped at 20 percent above the receiving lot's maximum floor area, or 30 percent in Commercial and Manufacturing Districts where the non-residential maximum FAR is 15.0 or more; larger transfers need the ZR 74-79 special permit. The transfer instrument and notices of restrictions are recorded, and a continuing maintenance program for the landmark is required.

mechanisms.name: Universal Affordability Preference
mechanisms.note: Additional residential floor area in R6 through R10 districts and their commercial equivalents when the added area is permanently affordable, replacing most Inclusionary Housing areas in December 2024.

mechanisms.name: Office to residential conversion
mechanisms.note: Non-residential buildings completed before 1991 may convert to residential under Article I Chapter 5 as amended in December 2024, with relief from some bulk and density rules; building code and light and air requirements still govern.
